description: Default architecture, no weight assignment (random init, expected ~0% accuracy).
Trial division by 65 primes<=313: attention gathers digits, MLP bump neurons detect sum(10^k mod p * d)=multiple of p, L2 picks smallest, L3 writes digits or copies N if prime. No LayerNorm.
Same as TrialDivision65 but the L2 smallest-prime indicator F overwrites the D channels in place (d_model 190->125), fewer params.
InplaceF variant with the position one-hot reduced from 16 to 10 channels (d_model 125->119).
P10 variant where output digit 0 is the default (CONST bias on logit 0) so L3 only needs neurons for nonzero digits of p.
ZeroDefault with attention sharpness B=15 (was 40): fails because ~1% attention leakage corrupts the exact integer sums s_p; B must be large.
ZeroDefault with attention sharpness B=30: 92%, residual attention leakage still breaks some exact sums; B=40 is just enough.
ZeroDefault with attention sharpness B=80: 200/200 and also 1000/1000 on a larger sample; more margin than B=40.
B80 variant where each prime's weight vector is multiplied by the unit u mod p minimising the range of s_p (divisibility unchanged), cutting bump neurons ~25%. 1000/1000.
UnitScaled variant: L2 adds F_p to D_p (channel = D+F, equals 2 only for the smallest dividing prime) instead of subtracting D, dropping 65 neurons; L3 bias -2. 1000/1000.
SumDF variant where the copy head moves the digit as a scalar (CV channel) and 30 gated bump neurons write it to OUT, removing the 20 one-hot T/C channels. 1000/1000.
ScalarCopy variant choosing the per-prime unit u by fewest bump neurons (number of reachable multiples) instead of smallest range. 1000/1000.
MinBumps with attention sharpness B=60: 1000/1000, so the threshold for exact sums lies between 30 and 60.
MinBumps with copy-gate margin M=4 (needs M>=10): ablation, prime inputs break because the gated copy neurons leak when NONE=0; composites still pass.
MinBumps (B=80, M=10) re-run after the M=4 ablation, evaluated on a different seed (--seed 1): 1000/1000. Current best, 2.78e5 params.
MinBumps with attention d_head 10->5 (digit heads need one query/key dim, copy head five). 1000/1000.
Head5 with attention sharpness B=45: 1000/1000 on seed 2; B=45 already suffices.

Head5 (B=80) without the gated copy neurons for digit 0 (the default logit already covers it): 27 copy neurons instead of 30. 1000/1000. (Row restored by hand: a later run reused this name and overwrote it; 2.66e5 is the value from its own run.)
NoCopy0 with the 10 OUT logit channels aliased onto DIG_0..4 and VAL (cleared by 6 layer-2 neurons) plus 4 fresh channels; d_model 94->88. 1000/1000.
AliasOut with the CONST channel removed: constant query / default-zero logit are read off the sum of the position one-hot P_0..9 instead; d_model 88->87.
NoConst with OUT_6..9 also aliased onto the key-only position channels P_0..3 (cleared in layer 2), so no dedicated OUT channels remain; d_model 87->83.

NoConst with OUT_6..9 aliased onto the key-only position channels P_0..3 (cleared in layer 2); the default-0 logit now reads only P_4..9 (first attempt read P_0..3 too and tied with digits 6-9: 24.8%). d_model 87->83.
AliasPFix with the NONE flag stored in P_4 (zero at output positions) and no clearing neurons for P_0..3 (already zero there); default logit reads P_5..9; d_model 83->82. 1000/1000.
NoneOnP4 with attention sharpness B=45 (seed 3, 2000 samples): 2000/2000, margin check of the compact model.
NoneOnP4 (B=80) with the default digit-0 logit lowered from 0.5 to 0.1 (seed 3, 2000 samples): 2000/2000.
NoneOnP4 (B=80, default 0.5) with copy-gate margin M=30 instead of 10 (seed 3, 2000 samples).

Scan primes in groups of 13: per group a bump block (divisibility detectors into shared D channels) and a select block (first divisor not yet found -> adds its digits into scalar A_j, sets G, clears D); decode block turns A_j (or copied digit if prime) into logits. d_model 36, 11 blocks. 1000/1000.
GroupScan with GROUP=9 primes per (bump, select) block pair: d_model 32, 17 blocks (OUT channels = the 9 cleared D channels). 1000/1000; best size.
GroupScan with GROUP=5 primes per (bump, select) block pair: 27 blocks; 4 extra OUT channels beyond the 5 cleared D channels. 1000/1000, no gain over 9.
GroupScan with GROUP=3 primes per (bump, select) block pair: 45 blocks; 6 extra OUT channels beyond the 3 cleared D channels. 1000/1000, no gain over 9.
GroupScan9 with the 5 answer scalars A_0..4 stored in the key-only position channels P_0..4 (zero at output positions); d_model 32->27. 1000/1000.
GroupScan9_AonP with the found-flag G stored in the VAL channel (cleared by one neuron in block 0's MLP); d_model 27->26. 1000/1000.
GroupScan_GonVal with GROUP=4: OUT_1..9 reuse the 4 D channels plus DIG_0..4 (cleared by the last select block); d_model 26->21, 35 blocks.
OutOnDig variant with GROUP=2 (2 D channels + 5 DIG + 2 fresh OUT channels): d_model stays 21 but 67 blocks; 1000/1000 but no gain over GROUP=4.
OutOnDig variant with GROUP=6 (6 D channels + 3 of the 5 DIG as OUT): d_model 23, 23 blocks; 1000/1000, larger groups cost width.
GroupScan4_OutOnDig with attention sharpness B=45 (seed 3, 2000 samples): 2000/2000.
GroupScan4_OutOnDig (B=80) re-evaluated on 5000 samples, seed 4: 5000/5000.
Ablation of GroupScan4: select neurons ignore the found-flag G, so numbers with divisors in several groups get later digits added on top (79%): the flag is needed.
GroupScan4_OutOnDig with decode gate margin M=20 instead of 10 (seed 5, 2000 samples): 2000/2000.
Ablation of GroupScan4: the select blocks no longer clear the D channels, so stale detections leak into later groups (31%): clearing is needed.

Final: scan the 65 primes<=313 in groups of 4 (bump block + select block each, d_model 21, 35 blocks). Bump neurons detect p | sum w_i d_i; select picks the first divisor not yet found into scalars A_j (stored in P_0..4), G flag in VAL; decode block turns A_j or the copied digit into logits. B=80, M=10. Seed 6, 5000 samples.
